name: Regions, Local Government, and Public Administration
summary: The 34 constituent Regions of the Concord, the four tiers of government, governing forms, the civil service, and integrity systems.

tiers.name: Concord
tiers.summary: Planetary tier; the ten enumerated powers.

tiers.name: Region
tiers.summary: Constituent units; health, education, housing, policing, land use, most taxation.

tiers.name: District
tiers.summary: Delivery tier; hospitals, schools, transit, utilities, planning.

tiers.name: Commune
tiers.summary: Neighbourhood tier; public space, local services, participatory allocation.

subsidiarityTest.name: Can the lower tier do this at all?
subsidiarityTest.summary: If yes, the enquiry usually ends.

subsidiarityTest.name: Does the problem cross the lower tier's boundary?
subsidiarityTest.summary: Atmosphere does; refuse collection does not.

subsidiarityTest.name: Would fragmentation impose costs the gain does not justify?
subsidiarityTest.summary: The only economic question, and deliberately the third one.

subsidiarityTest.name: Is the transfer reversible?
subsidiarityTest.summary: Irreversible centralization requires a Tier 2 amendment. About a third of competence disputes turn on this alone.

governingForms.name: Assembly-Executive
governingForms.summary: Elected assembly choosing a small collegial executive; commonest form.

governingForms.name: Assembly-Manager
governingForms.summary: Elected assembly sets policy, a professionally appointed manager executes on fixed contract. Highest service delivery, lowest public trust, unexplained.

governingForms.name: Direct-democratic
governingForms.summary: Frequent binding referendums with a small standing council.

governingForms.name: Delegate council
governingForms.summary: Governed by delegates from its Districts, with no separately elected regional body.

delegateSelectionMethods.name: Directly elected by the regional electorate
Selected by a sortition panel from a qualified pool
Rotated among District heads on a fixed schedule

regionalFloors.name: Government by an elected body
regionalFloors.summary: On a franchise no narrower than the Concord's.

regionalFloors.name: An independent audit body
regionalFloors.summary: One the regional government cannot appoint, fund, or discipline.

regionalFloors.name: Publication of records to the Concord standard

commune.localObjection: A Commune may compel a published response and public hearing on any District or Regional decision affecting it, but cannot block.

compacts.summary: Binding agreements between Regions requiring no planetary approval; must be registered and published.

civilService.entry: open competitive examination in all 41 registered languages
civilService.correctionNote: Corrected in Phase 6B: the Phase 4B figure of 43.1 million was arithmetically inconsistent with a population of 7.25 billion providing universal healthcare, education, and housing.

integritySystems.name: Open contracting by default
integritySystems.summary: Every contract at every tier published in machine-readable form within 30 days; no exemption threshold; price redaction capped at 3 years and itself published.

integritySystems.name: Asset and interest disclosure
integritySystems.summary: Annual, on leaving office, and again at 2 and 5 years afterwards — because the payoff usually arrives later than the favour.

integritySystems.name: The conflict registry
integritySystems.summary: Conflicts must be registered before acting; acting on an unregistered conflict is an offence independent of the underlying decision.

integritySystems.name: Two-key authorisation
integritySystems.summary: No single official may authorise a payment, licence, or consent above a modest threshold; the second key comes from a different reporting line and pairings are randomised.

integritySystems.name: Random deep audit
integritySystems.summary: 2% of public bodies selected annually by public verifiable lot for full unannounced audit. Purpose is uncertainty, not detection efficiency.

integritySystems.name: Protected disclosure
integritySystems.summary: Retaliation is criminal with reversed burden of proof: adverse treatment within 3 years of disclosure is presumed retaliatory. Anonymous disclosure protected equally.

integritySystems.name: Cooling-off with continuing salary
integritySystems.summary: 10 years for office heads, 5 for exposed posts and Board members, paid — because an unpaid restriction restricts only those who cannot afford it.

integrityOutcomes.note: Corruption is small, prosecuted, and mostly petty. The Audit Service states in every annual report that the residual rate is not zero and will not become zero. Perception exceeds measured reality and rises with distance from the resident.

transparency.failureReportingNote: Bodies that publish no failures are audited on that basis; a flawless self-report is treated as evidence of inattention or concealment.

digitalAdministration.rationale: A state that cannot read its own systems cannot be audited, and a state that cannot leave a supplier is governed by it.
automatedDecisionConstraints: an identified human official is accountable for every decision affecting rights
the reasons requirement applies identically to automated decisions
any person may demand non-automated reconsideration

knownWeaknesses.name: Interregional inequality
knownWeaknesses.summary: Floors without ceilings lets wealthy Regions race ahead; equalization narrows but does not close the gap.

knownWeaknesses.name: Capacity asymmetry
knownWeaknesses.summary: Small Regions cannot staff competences they legally hold; Concord-funded shared services are criticised as centralization by the back door.

knownWeaknesses.name: Comparability distortion
knownWeaknesses.summary: Published league tables reward measurable outcomes and can starve the unmeasurable.

knownWeaknesses.name: Orbital Territory anomaly
knownWeaknesses.summary: A Region defined by installations rather than territory strains every assumption in Article 3.

knownWeaknesses.name: Boundary conservatism
knownWeaknesses.summary: Founding watershed boundaries no longer match settlement in three Regions; correction is slow.

knownWeaknesses.name: Compact opacity
knownWeaknesses.summary: 340 compacts are published but rarely read, and can shape obligations without planetary debate.

knownWeaknesses.name: Documentation burden
knownWeaknesses.summary: 9% of civil service time goes to producing reasons; permanently contested.

knownWeaknesses.name: Rotation versus expertise
knownWeaknesses.summary: Five-year rotation removes mastery from the posts where mastery is most useful.

knownWeaknesses.name: Perception gap
knownWeaknesses.summary: Trust in the planetary tier is lower than its measured performance; unexplained and unfixed.

knownWeaknesses.name: Publication without readership
knownWeaknesses.summary: The Concord has solved disclosure and not solved attention. A right of access is worth what someone's willingness to read is worth.
